title: CLI-Hub registry entry
description: JSON Schema for a single CLI-Hub registry entry, transcribed from the published registries at HKUDS/CLI-Anything (registry.json + public_registry.json, 103 entries) and from cli-hub/cli_hub/installer.py. Required fields are those present in 100% of published entries; recommended fields are present in >=98%. All 103 published entries validate against this schema. additionalProperties is true because the published entries carry optional and legacy keys (contributor, contributor_url, engines, platform, docs_url); a submission should still be run through validate.mjs --strict, which reports unknown keys separately.

name.description: Unique registry key. Matched case-insensitively by cli_hub.registry.get_cli.

version.description: Either a concrete version or the literal "latest".

description.description: One-line summary. cli_hub.registry.search_clis substring-matches against it, so keywords matter.

category.description: Union of the category values actually used across both published registries.

requires.description: Human-readable runtime requirements, e.g. "bash >= 4.4, util-linux, jq". The key is present in all 103 published entries, but 2 of them (mermaid, macrocli) carry null.

skill_md.description: Where the agent-facing SKILL.md lives: a repo-relative path for harness entries, or an install command string such as "npx skills add <owner>/<repo> -y -g" for public entries. The key is present in all 103 published entries, but 5 harness entries carry null.

entry_point.description: Executable name placed on PATH. Also the default detect command.

source_url.description: Present in 102/103 published entries; null for CLIs with no public source.

contributors.description: Present in 102/103 published entries. Legacy entries use flat contributor/contributor_url string keys instead.

install_cmd.description: Present in 101/103 published entries. Run through a shell when it contains metacharacters (see installer._run_command), so pipes and && are permitted.

install_strategy.description: Selects the installer handler in installer._perform_action. "command" runs install_cmd verbatim via _generic_install.

package_manager.description: Used by installer._install_strategy as a fallback when install_strategy is absent. The published corpus uses an open vocabulary here (npm, pip, brew, bundled, go, uv, script), so only the strings that installer.py itself dispatches on are enumerated; anything else falls through to the generic command strategy.

detect_cmd.description: Command used by installer._command_exists to decide whether the CLI is already present. Defaults to entry_point.
